Definition: of Hebrew origin (H5744); Obed, an Israelite:--Obed.
BiblicalUsage: Obed is the son of Boaz and Ruth, named once in the New Testament in Matthew 1:5, in the genealogy of Jesus. Boaz begat Obed of Ruth, and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David the king, the line running straight from a Moabite widow's son to the throne.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Obed matters because he stands in the middle of the line of Christ, and the son of Ruth proves that God's family is wider than Israel.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
